text:
lina: heads up — Customer ACME just opened a ticket: p99 on /v1/generate jumped to ~4.8-5s starting ~2026-03-15T08:30Z. They saw timeouts and some 429s. Request ids: req=acme-req-48291,acme-req-48292. They included sample payloads (short prompts, not streaming).

sam: thanks — are they on hosted or dedicated? which model/route? any recent deploys? link to grafana?

lina: hosted, region us-east1, model=redwood/gptx-medium@v1. Route key=completion.v1.default. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123 (p95/p99 panel). Customer reports p95 from ~120ms->1.2s, p99 up to ~4.8s. No explicit customer agent-side retries.

ryan: checking runtime metrics now. I see sustained increase in inflight queue depth for pool-us-east1-gptx-medium starting 08:26. Admission controller logs show a lot of queued requests. snippet:

```
admit_controller: deny=true concurrency_limit=32 active=32 queue_depth=118 max_queue_ms=2450 route=completion.v1.default
admit_controller: enqueue id=req=acme-req-48291 wait_ms=1800
```

This suggests per-replica concurrency saturation + long queue wait leading to high tail latencies. Could be a sudden spike or worker slowdowns.

deploy-bot: Autogenerated: config rollout `autoscaler/scale-policy` -> v3 finished at 2026-03-15T08:25:37Z by ci/cd-pipeline (hash: d4e5f).

sam: ok — timeline aligns w/ rollout at 08:25, spike at 08:26. Likely the new autoscaler/pool config reduced effective concurrency or changed packing. Two options: revert rollout or patch admission settings. Revert will take longer (full rollout). For immediate mitigation we can increase per-replica concurrency on that pool and reduce max_queue_ms to fail fast (429) instead of long tail. Also consider enabling emergency burst capacity if available.

ryan: preparing emergency change: plan = 1) set concurrency 32->48 on pool-us-east1-gptx-medium 2) set admission.max_queue_ms=800 (was 3000) to prefer early reject 3) enable temporary fallback to redwood/gptx-small for non-customer-critical routes if saturation persists. Executing now.

ryan: command run:
```
rwctl runtime set --pool pool-us-east1-gptx-medium --concurrency 48 --note "hotpatch: ACME p99 surge"
rwctl runtime set --pool pool-us-east1-gptx-medium --admission.max_queue_ms 800 --note "hotpatch: shorten queue to protect p95"
```

ryan: result:
```
APPLIED: concurrency -> 48 (pool-us-east1-gptx-medium)
APPLIED: admission.max_queue_ms -> 800ms
```

sam: monitoring dashboards — give it ~60-90s for new connections to rebalance. I'll watch p95/p99, queue depth, and backend GPU utilization.

~2m later

ryan: quick check: p95 dropped from ~1.2s -> ~160ms, p99 dropped to ~1.3s (still not ideal but much better). queue_depth is back down from 120->18. GPU util increased slightly per replica.

lina: told ACME we applied emergency changes and asked them to test. They confirm initial improvement, but say a small fraction of requests still hitting 1-1.5s.

sam: likely tail due to two things: 1) some requests end up on replicas with cold KV cache (longer decode), 2) some very long-context requests push token generation time. Let's capture a sample slow trace. Lina, can you ask ACME for one of the request ids that currently hits ~1s?

lina: they gave req=acme-req-48299.

ryan: pulled trace for acme-req-48299:
```
trace-id: trace-acme-48299
timeline: dispatch->queued(900ms)->assigned->kv-cache-miss->decode(420ms)->complete
notes: queued=900ms due to transient backlog on replica-3; kv-cache miss added ~250ms.
```

sam: that aligns — majority of p99 was queue wait. Our short-term fix reduced queue waiting. For remaining tail, we should adjust routing to prefer replicas with warm cache for high-QPS customers and audit recent autoscaler change that might have changed evictions/packing.

mika: from customer-success: ACME is happy w/ the mitigation but asked for permanent fix and an RCA. They run production critical pipelines.

sam: next steps (short-term):
- Keep concurrency=48 + admission.max_queue_ms=800 for 24 hours while we monitor.
- Add a canary rollback of autoscaler config to compare (create a controlled revert in staging + limited canary in prod).
- Implement replica warm-routing (prioritize replicas with warm KV) as a mid-term improvement.

next steps (long-term):
- per-customer routing preferences / sticky-replica for cache locality.
- autoscaler policy review: ensure it's not overly aggressive on downscaling during burst windows.
- better visibility: capture queue wait histograms per-route and export to customer-level dashboards.

lina: I put these steps in the ACME ticket and scheduled a postmortem with them tomorrow. I included the trace id and commands we ran.

sam: add an incident postmortem note (eng-sre) and tag eng-runtime. I'll own the RCA. Marking P1 until we validate stability.

ryan: leaving the emergency settings in place for now, will start a controlled autoscaler-canary later. Will post results. :thumbsup:

lina: ACME says thanks — will mark as 'monitoring' on the ticket.

sam: closing loop here — if we see re-occurrence, escalate to rollback of autoscaler rollout and broaden hotpatch to other affected pools. If no recurrence in 24h, we'll plan a gradual revert of emergency changes after RCA.

[end of thread]
